rows.verified: Employers and people in control of premises must identify and assess sources of legionella risk.
The risk assessment is the dutyholder's responsibility and should be completed or supported by a competent person.
A competent responsible person with sufficient authority, knowledge, skills and experience must be appointed to control identified risks.
Water systems should be designed, maintained and operated to prevent or adequately control legionella growth and multiplication.
A written control scheme should describe the system, responsibilities, operating controls, precautions, checks and check frequencies.
Controls should address spray release, stagnation, favourable temperatures, system cleanliness, treatment and monitoring.
Where five or more employees are present, significant findings and prevention or control steps must be recorded.
Risk assessments and control performance should be reviewed regularly and when systems, responsibilities or operating conditions change.
Controls depend on the water system, temperatures, aerosol generation, stagnation, users, susceptibility and operating regime.
Legionella evidence is water-system-, operation- and population-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
The Work at Height Regulations apply where a fall from one level to another could cause personal injury.
Work at height must be properly planned, appropriately supervised and carried out by competent people.
Dutyholders must select the right type of equipment for the work and the assessed risk.
Risk assessment must cover work organisation, competence, suitable equipment and the controls needed to prevent injury.
Risks from fragile surfaces, openings and edges must be properly managed.
Work-at-height equipment must be appropriately inspected and maintained.
The control hierarchy is to avoid work at height where possible, prevent falls, then minimise fall distance and consequences.
Ladders are appropriate only where risk assessment shows higher-protection equipment is not justified because of low risk and short duration or unalterable features.
Controls depend on task, height, duration, access, surface strength, weather, rescue arrangements and worker competence.
Work-at-height evidence is task-, equipment- and condition-specific and is not an exact parcel-level fall probability.
